newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares fall, seen tracking sideways.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares fall, seen tracking sideways.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 1.7 percent on Friday on what traders said was a technical reaction after Thursday's four percent jump.
The SBI index fell 23.11 points or 1.7 percent to close at 1,333.14, ending a three-day losing streak. Over the week as a whole, the index still managed a gain of 4.62 percent.
Overall six shares fell, eight rose and one was flat, while 12 were untraded. Turnover fell to 66.7 million tolars from 102.7 million.
"I don't expect major changes until the end of this month, unless some fresh information about foreign investors becomes available," said Bojan Sekavcnik, a trader at brokerage PM & A.
He added that foreign capital was urgently needed to help the fledgling market stabilise.
In February the central bank restricted international investors' access to the market by ordering them to open custody accounts with local banks. Since then, the index has lost 19.47 percent.

Newcomer Radenska, a maker of mineral water whose shares debuted on the Ljubljana market on Thursday, was the day's most active share and the biggest gainer, firming 3.63 percent to 1,999 tolars on volume of 10,310 shares for total turnover of 20.2 million tolars.
"Most traders see Radenska's shares as a good investment at current prices, which are considered to be relatively low concerning their future perspective," Sekavcnik said.
Health resort operator Terme Catez led the day's decliners, tumbling 8.24 percent to 12,020 tolars on volume of 332 shares.
